questions.question: When is a security checklist item meaningfully complete?
options: When a security product has been purchased
When the control has a named threat, enforced boundary, owner, and evidence that it works
When the item appears in a compliance template
When the implementation has no open bugs
questions.explanation: A useful check connects risk to enforcement and proof. Product ownership or documentation alone does not show that the harmful path is actually blocked or recoverable.

questions.question: A user has a valid session and requests an order owned by another tenant. Which control must make the decisive check?
options: TLS certificate validation
Client-side route visibility
Server-side authorization using the actor, action, tenant, and resource
Database encryption at rest
questions.explanation: Authentication proves who holds the session; it does not grant access to every object. The server must authorize this action on this specific tenant resource.

questions.question: An API receives 10,000 requests per second and 1% are suspicious. How many requests per second enter the suspicious-request stream?
questions.explanation: 10,000 multiplied by 0.01 equals 100 requests per second. A small percentage can still create a continuous operational workload.

questions.question: A policy service times out during a request to change payout details. What is the safest default?
options: Allow the change because the user is already signed in
Retry without a deadline until the service responds
Deny or return an unavailable outcome because a trustworthy authorization decision is missing
Move the authorization check into the browser
questions.explanation: A high-impact action should not silently become allowed when its policy dependency fails. A bounded unavailable response preserves the authorization invariant.

questions.question: Which event is safest and most useful for investigating a denied sensitive read?
options: Actor, action, resource identifier, outcome, policy version, time, and request ID
The full session token and password
The complete customer record and request body
Only a message saying something failed
questions.explanation: Structured decision context supports correlation and policy review without turning the evidence store into a collection of credentials and sensitive payloads.

questions.question: Why can a failed security-event pipeline be serious even when customer requests still succeed?
options: It automatically disables encryption at rest
It removes timely evidence for detection, containment, and investigation
It guarantees every request is unauthorized
It changes every API response to a timeout
questions.explanation: Prevention and evidence are separate controls. Lost or delayed events can increase attacker dwell time and make it difficult to prove scope or respond correctly.
